newsitem.title: UK: No respite for NWE fuel oil as crude losses extend.
newsitem.headline: No respite for NWE fuel oil as crude losses extend.

text.p: Tumbling crude pulled the fuel oil market lower on Wednesday. Activity also slumped as buyers played a "wait and see" game on how far crude would fall.

High sulphur barges slumped sharply in the morning in very quiet trade with deals done between $114.25 fob ARA to $111 a tonne. Shipper demand picked up marginally in the afternoon, helping barges crawl back to $112-114, some $4 off Tuesday's levels.
Cargoes were also knocked lower during the course of the day. A utility was heard looking for material at $114.50 cif NWE, but was thought to be after lower numbers in the afternoon.
Supplies were judged to be fair and concrete buying absent.
"Buyers are waiting to pounce when they judge prices to have bottomed out. With crude continuing to fall that has not happened yet," said one dealer.

The low sulphur sector, seen by traders to have more fundamental strength than high sulphur, was not immune to the southward draw of crude. A deal was thought done, but was being kept discreet. Swap talk was down to $128-129 fob NWE for December and $126-127 for January.
